audience_moment.emotional_tension: They want the invitation and they're afraid of the version of themselves that has to show up for it.
audience_moment.observable_behaviour: They put the phone face-down on their knee, pick the mug up, put it back down untouched, then turn the phone over and read the message again.
audience_moment.private_worry: That saying yes commits them to being a fun, available person on a set date, and if it's flat then, it will have been their fault for agreeing.
audience_moment.situation: Saturday 11:20am, a text from someone they've met twice asks 'are you around this weekend? we should do something', and they read it on the sofa with a mug balanced on the armrest.

critic.evidence: "phone face-down on my knee. mug up. mug down. untouched." and "not a no. just not yet a yes."
critic.rewrite_notes: Nearly there. "not a no" is slightly more articulate than the sofa moment; keep it but consider a blunter payoff like "still don't know what i'm doing." No structural faults.
critic.sendability_who: Someone 18-30 sending it to the friend who watched them agonise over a new-friend text, or to the new friend as a soft, funny yes.

audience_moment.emotional_tension: They want to be in the room and they're waiting for a permission to enter that nobody knows they need.
audience_moment.observable_behaviour: They open the dishwasher, stand holding the plate, wait for a gap in the talk, half-lift a hand, then close the dishwasher and go back to their room without saying anything.
audience_moment.private_worry: That walking in and leaving without a word will read as cold or sulky, when really they just couldn't find a door into the conversation.
audience_moment.situation: Thursday 8:40pm in a shared kitchen, four people from the flat and two of their friends are talking, and they walk in to put a plate in the dishwasher.

critic.evidence: "close the dishwasher like you meant to" and "laugh a beat late at something you missed" - exact, unshowy, no diagnosis.
critic.rewrite_notes: Almost nothing fails. Items 2 and 3 sit closest together; if trimmed, make one of them a later moment (e.g. reheating the plate later) to widen the timeline. Closing line slightly long.
critic.sendability_who: Someone 18-30 sending it to the flatmate who always seems to vanish after putting a plate away, or to the friend who does it themselves and needs the reframe.

5. close the dishwasher like you meant to
6. say night to no one in particular
7. replay the exit in your room
payload.closing: you were not being cold. you were looking for a door and the room was full of people standing in it.
